CausalChain: Dietary polyphenols -> Reduce hepatic oxidative stress -> Potentiate hepatic PPARβ/δ activity -> Upregulate lipogenic genes leading to increased synthesis of PC (18:0/18:1) -> Circulating PC (18:0/18:1) reaches muscle -> Activates muscle PPARα -> Promotes muscle fatty acid uptake and oxidation -> Decreases circulating triglycerides and lipid overload
Hypothesis: Dietary supplementation with polyphenol-rich extracts enhances hepatic PPARβ/δ activity to increase PC (18:0/18:1) production, which in turn activates muscle PPARα, promoting muscle fatty acid oxidation and thereby mitigating dyslipidemia and hepatic steatosis.
Abstract: This study proposes a novel mechanism whereby dietary polyphenols enhance hepatic PPARβ/δ activity, leading to increased synthesis of specific phosphatidylcholine species, notably PC (18:0/18:1). The secreted PC (18:0/18:1) acts as a lipid mediator in the periphery, particularly in skeletal muscle, by promoting fatty acid uptake and oxidation through activation of muscle PPARα. Enhanced fatty acid utilization in muscle may alleviate systemic lipid overload, improve dyslipidemia, and counteract hepatic steatosis. This hepatic–muscle cross‐talk mechanism offers a potentially innovative strategy for combating metabolic syndrome and its complications.
